## 席位核对

**L1 verdict: ACCEPT** — head `a407b4dad645ecced7167efaccfbe8091a443281` (the head comment 6933264312 declares final). Card #34502, area o2-S. Read at 2026-11-17T00:06Z.

### Checklist conclusions

- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. One closing line for the card, after the attribution lines; no closing verb sits next to any other number. The card's done-when holds at head:
  - A reader of `lanes/l2-review.md` alone opens the seat at the default tier and reviews through one fresh sub-agent per head (L6–7).
  - The in-seat trap is named once, at its home: `contract-review.md` L38 says 席位开席即调 Skill 恒不合. The other file points to it (`(../contract-review.md)` on L7).
- **Premise, and the card's stop condition.** The trap is real at `main`: `scripts/pm/verify-review-tier.mjs` L82 and L93–94 list `Agent`/`Task`/`Workflow`/`SendMessage` and `/^Skill$/` as hand-off tools, so a transcript that calls `Skill` is refused. The card would stop on a false reading of its one unmeasured point (whether a default-tier seat's at-tier sub-agent is served at tier). That point reads true on GitHub: `l2-review#4` (an `os-steve` seat) has posted `Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS records on #33995 (comment 6932506491) and #34489 (comment 6932783796), and the writer posts that tier only with a verified `--tier-evidence`.
- **Scope.** Two `.claude/**` files, +5 / −5. The branch carries one merge of `origin/main` (`a407b4da`, after #34485 landed). The three-dot diff holds only these five line pairs. In `lanes/l2-review.md`, the #34485 deletion and routing section are kept as `main` has them.
- **Changeset.** Not owed: `.claude/**` publishes nothing. `skip-changeset` is set, and `Check Changeset` is `success`/`skipped`, not red.
- **Rule text, read line by line.**
  - `l2-review.md` L6: the seating account can reach `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, and the seat session itself runs at the default tier. This is the maintainer's 「重开一条 opus 审核席」 as the card quotes it.
  - L7: one fresh read-only sub-agent per submitted head, at tier. The old 「L2 子代理恒契约审核档」 survives as 达档.
  - `contract-review.md` L36–38: the session-transcript road narrows to card threads; the seat trap is stated; the sub-agent output file stays the evidence.
- **Paydown: each cut keeps a home.**
  - `node scripts/pm/` prefix dropped → the bare name is already used at L45 (`record-recognisers.mjs --brief-template`), and L46 refers to `--template`.
  - `~/.claude/projects/*/<id>.jsonl` → the verifier header, which L38 names (`verify-review-tier.mjs` L21–24, "The transcript it reads", spells the path).
  - 「卡线程或席内 L2」 → 卡线程, with the in-seat case now stated outright.
- **Line rules at head.** `check-skill-line-ratchet` passes: `l2-review.md` 22/22, `contract-review.md` 63/63, headroom 0, no raise. Edited lines are 103–118 bytes. `check-skill-id-lint` reads `118 file(s) clean`.
- **Gates.** Check-runs on this head: 47 runs, 23 `success`, 24 `skipped`, 0 failure, 0 pending. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` aggregate, `PR-body guards` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are all `success`. The local 19-command ledger was run on this head. I take the check-runs as the gate record.

### Accepted deviations / observations

- O1 (for L2 ④ to weigh): the new L7 bans 席内达档审 in the sense of "the seat's own session". AGENTS.md L291 uses the same words for Tier S (席内达档 L2 审核落地), meaning "seat-owned, not human". `contract-review.md` L33 already uses 席内 in the in-seat sense, and the pointer on L7 resolves the reading, so this is not a rework item. A spelling such as 席会话自身达档审 would remove the collision.
- O2 (nit): the PR body says the bare script name sits at "lines 48 and 51". At this head it is L45 (and L46 for `--template`), shifted by the main merge. The survival claim itself holds.
- O3: the card's 速读 says the landing is Tier H with an approval. The tool reading below is Tier S, because the only governed surface is `.claude/**`. The PR body's 速读 already says Tier S.

### Contract review (L2) owed?

**Yes, and still open.** `.claude/**` is governed rules text, and the pm-dispatch root is always at contract tier, so it owes `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. At the time of reading, this head has only a claim: `l2-review#4`, comment 6933297208, head `a407b4da…`. There is no PASS record yet. The independence pair holds: the implementing card-thread session (`session_01ADHkmPJMYf74i7NNkxcVQn`) differs from the claiming L2 session.

### Landing tier

`node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34510` reads **GOVERNED, Tier S**: `.claude/**` is hit twice. Size is +5 / −5. Once an at-tier PASS stands on this same head, the owning area lands it: ready, then the merge queue, with every check green. This review does not flip ready, arm auto-merge, or merge.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a407b4dad645ecced7167efaccfbe8091a443281`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/l2-review.md + none

### ① Derived judgments

Net diff against the PR base (`0c7869c0`, the head's second parent): 2 files, +5 / -5, both under `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/`. No code, no schema, no generated output, no changeset. Both files keep their line counts (22 and 63).

- Published accept sets and public surface: none touched. Right: nothing under `packages/**` or any `exports` map is in the diff.
- Rule-text change 1 (`lanes/l2-review.md` line 6): the L2 seat session moves from "a session of an account that reaches `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`" to "the account can reach the tier; the seat session itself runs at the default tier". Right: it matches the maintainer words quoted in the card body and the standing seat-tier policy in `execution-duties.md` (seats at the default tier, the review tier taken only through an isolated sub-agent or a card thread).
- Rule-text change 2 (`lanes/l2-review.md` line 7): one fresh read-only sub-agent per submitted head renders the at-tier review; the seat never reviews at tier in its own session. Right: `verify-review-tier.mjs` judges the transcript of the run that reviewed, and its header names exactly this road ("the review's own sub-agent file, or reviews in a fresh agent").
- Rule-text change 3 (`contract-review.md` lines 36-38): the session-transcript road for `--tier-evidence` narrows in the rules text from "card thread or in-seat L2" to "card thread", and one clause states that a seat's own transcript never meets the condition. Right as a rule: the verifier is unchanged and still fails closed, so the text only removes a road that never passed for a seat. No gate reads this sentence; no machine accept set moves.
- The two cuts that paid for the words (the `node scripts/pm/` prefix on the template command, and the literal transcript path) remove no fact: the bare script name already stands at lines 45-46 of the same file, and the transcript path lives in the header of `scripts/pm/verify-review-tier.mjs`, which line 38 names.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no — correct. The diff is `.claude/**` rules text only and publishes nothing; no changeset is owed, the PR carries `skip-changeset`, and `Check Changeset` is skipped on that label. No semver level applies.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on the head: 47, all completed; every one is success or skipped, none failed, none pending. `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are success, which covers the line ratchet and the self-tests that read these two files.
- Dev deviation (script path shortened, transcript path dropped for a pointer): accepted, see ① last bullet.
- Open question 1 (serial with #34485): answered, option A was taken. The head is a merge of main after #34485 landed; the net diff against the base is still only this PR's five lines, and #34485's routing section and its deletion read as main has them.
- Open question 2 (is a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` sub-agent started from a default-tier seat served exactly at the tier): the PR body says the L2 seat's first run measured it. That reading is not in the review inputs (no record on the card or the PR carries it), so it is not relied on here. It is answered by this record's own posting: this review was rendered by exactly such a sub-agent, and the write tool admits the record only if `verify-review-tier.mjs` passes on its output file. Option A holds: if that write is refused, the card's stop applies (`premise_still_valid: false`) and this PASS covers nothing.
- Landing tier: the card body says "Tier H"; the register reads `.claude/**` as Tier S (AGENTS.md), as the PR body and the final-head comment say. The card sentence is stale wording, no effect on the diff.
- PR body cites the bare script name at lines 48 and 51 of `contract-review.md`; at this head they are lines 45 and 46. The tree is what was judged.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay author to name.
- SQL push-down: no code in the diff; nothing to check.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/l2-review.md` — holds.
- Against the card's acceptance ("a reader of `l2-review.md` alone opens an L2 seat on the default tier and reviews through one fresh sub-agent per head"): lines 6-7 say both, and the pointer `../contract-review.md` resolves from `lanes/` to the home of the evidence rule. The card's change list also asked this file to say that the sub-agent's output file is the `--tier-evidence`; the PR leaves that to the pointer, since `contract-review.md` line 36-37 already says it. Accepted deviation: the Done-when is met and the fact has one home.
- Against the code it cites: `judgeReviewTranscript` refuses any assistant turn whose served model is not the tier, and any turn that calls `Skill`, `Agent`, `Task`, `Workflow`, `SendMessage` or a hand-off connector tool. A default-tier seat session therefore fails on its first turn, and a fresh sub-agent that calls none of these passes. The rule sends the reader down the only road the verifier admits.
- Tried to break it: (a) delta reviews. "delta 归原 L2 审核者" (line 17) still works, because the reviewer of record is the adopting seat (`Reviewed-by:`, "子代理记采纳它的席位"), and a delta head is a new submitted head, so it gets its own fresh sub-agent. (b) Reviews below tier. SKILL.md keeps `TIER_DEFAULT` reviews with the lanes, never the L2 seat, so "every submitted head ⇒ an at-tier sub-agent" leaves no head uncovered. (c) Independence. The sub-agent is a different agent from the drafter and is fed the brief, not the seat's conclusions; unchanged.

`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md` — holds.
- The trap is named once, at the evidence rule, and `l2-review.md` points at it, as the card's Done-when requires. The sub-agent road (explicit tier model, output file as evidence) and the "refused ⇒ rerun the sub-agent, never rename the tier" clause are intact.
- Against the verifier: the card-thread condition (no other agent, no message, no `Skill`) still summarises `handsWorkToAnotherAgent`; the conclusion that a seat's own transcript never passes is true on this tree, and under this PR for a second reason the text does not need to state (the seat runs at the default tier, so the model check refuses first).
- Tried to break it: lane seats that self-review at tier (line 16) lose the "in-seat" session road in the text. They never had it in practice: a lane seat runs dev agents and is held at the default tier by `execution-duties.md`, so its transcript refused already. No head is left without a road.

N1 (nit) — `contract-review.md` line 38 gives the `Skill` call as the reason a seat's transcript never qualifies. That is the measured reason for a project seat; a seat opened by a typed slash command may hold no `Skill` tool call, and its transcript still refuses because the seat is not at the tier. The conclusion is right either way. Accepted as written.

N2 (nit) — `l2-review.md` line 6 writes "默认档" where the rest of the rulebook writes the constant `TIER_DEFAULT` or "默认判断档" (`execution-duties.md`), and `platform-readings.md` uses "默认档" for the harness default. Readable in context; a later prose pass may align the term.

N3 (nit) — outside the diff, the header of `verify-review-tier.mjs`, the refusal text in `post-stamped.mjs` and a note in `dispatch-gates.mjs` still mention the in-seat session road. They describe what the verifier would accept from a session wholly at the tier, which stays mechanically true, and they fail closed. A follow-up card may align the wording; ⛔ not in this PR, since those are code files and would move the head.
